# ellmos ControlCenter MCP

> MCP control-plane server for local MCP stack discovery, MCP profile inspection, capability bundle recommendation, policy audits, i18n-aware outputs, a local dashboard, and a policy-gated, audited gateway that lists and invokes tools on backend MCP servers the host has not loaded. It prepares configuration and does not change running sessions.

Last-checked: 2026-09-26
Test status: 261/261 Vitest tests passing (100% green)
Canonical repository: https://github.com/ellmos-ai/ellmos-controlcenter-mcp
npm package: https://www.npmjs.com/package/ellmos-controlcenter-mcp
MCP registry name: io.github.ellmos-ai/ellmos-controlcenter-mcp
License: MIT
Attribution: NOTICE
Language: TypeScript
Runtime: Node.js >=20

## Summary

ellmos ControlCenter MCP is an alpha-stage Model Context Protocol server for local MCP administration. It discovers local MCP repositories and registered stack compositions, reads MCP profile files, resolves inherited profile configurations, recommends profiles and capability bundles for tasks, runs initial profile policy audits, builds local server catalogs, probes real MCP tool lists from local repositories or profiles, assigns tools to capability bundles, supports maintained output text sets for `de`, `en`, `es`, `zh`, `ja`, and `ru`, and can start a local dashboard.

It is useful for local MCP stack visibility, profile management, and for keeping a small loaded profile while remaining able to reach the other servers on demand. It is not a hardened security gateway: the gateway forwards tool calls under a pattern-based policy and an audit log, but authentication, risk-class enforcement, and hard isolation are still planned rather than implemented.

Host registers: seven read-only tools expose this machine's project locks, agent-neutral permission register, pending decision list, policy registry, strategic-plan index, and resource inventory of systems and installed software. They never write — no lock is set, renewed or released, no decision answered, and no policy, plan or BYUM candidate adopted — and they fail closed, reporting source-specific availability rather than silently empty data. Lock, permission and decision tools delegate every rule to the host's canonical Python modules instead of reimplementing it; the policy side of the governance view is validated only through `PolicyRegistry.load()`; the plan side projects a fixed scalar allowlist from the existing `_PLANS` index; the resource tools are a plain read-only mirror of `.SYNC/_inventory/inventory.db`, with register authority sitting explicitly with the ControlRoom programme, not this server. All stay inert until their respective `ELLMOS_*` variables are configured.

Scope boundary: ControlCenter is read-mostly outside the gateway. Its write actions are limited to generating an MCP configuration file, writing a catalog file, appending to the gateway audit log, and — via the dashboard, with confirmation and backup — toggling servers in a profile file. It never changes a running session. Since 2026-08-16 it does sit in the request path for one explicit case: `controlcenter_invoke` executes a single tool on another MCP server, gated by `data/gateway-policy.json` and recorded in an audit log. Only servers declared by the configured MCP root or a named profile can be addressed. It owns no domain data: policies, decisions, plans, memory, tasks, tickets, and automations belong to other components.

Gateway: `controlcenter_list_available_tools` reports the tools of servers the host has not loaded; `controlcenter_invoke` runs one of them and returns the result. The connection is opened per call and closed again, so no backend process is left running. Fail-closed: a server that cannot be asked is reported as unreachable with an unknown tool count, never as a server without tools, and a malformed policy file refuses every call instead of falling back to allow-all. A tool error reported by the target is kept distinct from a gateway failure, because the call did arrive. Argument values never reach the audit log.

Gateway hardening: forwarded payloads are treated as untrusted foreign data. Results are redacted recursively before reaching the caller, and the number of replaced values is reported; narrow credential patterns are replaced everywhere, while key-based wiping applies only to structured metadata so that requested file contents are never silently altered. Finite budgets bound request size, response size, nesting depth, content blocks, and concurrent invocations; oversized arguments are refused rather than shortened, while oversized answers are truncated and flagged. Remote targets must be HTTPS unless they are on loopback, redirects are refused, and an optional host allowlist narrows this further. Forwarded content is marked as data rather than as instructions.

Tool catalog hardening: `controlcenter_list_tools`, bundle assignment, catalog building, and the dashboard scan use a default limit of four concurrent probes and a 1 MiB aggregate response budget. Overrides are bounded to 1–32 probes and 1 KiB–16 MiB. Targets skipped or cut off by a budget are returned as `incomplete` with an unknown tool count. Header/auth contract `ellmos.tool-scan-headers.v1` passes profile-defined SSE/Streamable HTTP headers through the installed SDK transport to the event-stream GET and MCP message requests; redirects are refused, errors mask configured secrets, and every transport is closed.

MCP catalog capability tags: `mcps.catalog.v1.json` remains backward-compatible when `capability_tags` is absent. When present, it must use `ellmos.capability-tags.v1` and a unique string tag list; tags are normalized and exposed read-only. Invalid types or duplicates make the catalog `invalid`, and tags never grant installation or execution authority.

## Governance & Runtime Invariants

1. `INV-LOCAL-01`: Local-First & Explicit Egress (dashboard loopback binding, no telemetry or background egress; explicit gateway calls may reach remote HTTPS backends).
2. `INV-GATE-02`: Fail-Closed Gateway Policy Guard (data/gateway-policy.json enforcement; denies unknown/invalid).
3. `INV-SUB-03`: Ephemeral Child Process Boundaries (connect-per-call stdio lifecycle; zero lingering background processes).
4. `INV-SCRUB-04`: Bounded Result Redaction & Finite Budgets (narrow credential patterns throughout results, key wiping only in structured metadata, 256KB request / 1MB response caps).
5. `INV-PRIV-05`: Non-Elevation / RunAsInvoker (operates strictly in unprivileged user space).
6. `INV-LOCK-06`: Canonical Multi-Agent Lock Awareness (respects LOCK*.txt, LOCK.user.*, LOCK.until.* fail-closed).
7. `INV-PERM-07`: Nearest Permission Register Introspection (evaluates LOCK.permissions.json up directory trees).
8. `INV-GOV-08`: Read-Only Host Governance Federation (mirrors decisions, policies, plans without mutating).
9. `INV-SYNC-09`: Cloud-Sync Conflict Hardening (.gitignore hardened against sync conflicts and lock files).
10. `INV-SLA-10`: 48-Hour Response & 5-Day Triage SLA (security vulnerability response commitments).

## Tools

- `controlcenter_status`: show stack, profile, and detected-server status.
- `controlcenter_actual_self_receipt`: emit a short-lived signed native ControlCenter runtime receipt when host-local configuration is present; no trust or routing activation.
- `controlcenter_get_language`: show the current ControlCenter output language.
- `controlcenter_set_language`: set the ControlCenter output language for this running server instance.
- `controlcenter_list_local_servers`: scan local MCP repositories below the configured MCP root and enrich each with kind and persistent-state facts from `mcps.catalog.v1.json`.
- `controlcenter_describe_mcp`: describe one MCP server from `mcps.catalog.v1.json` — kind, namespace, npm name, per-namespace state ownership, wrapping, and composition; degrades to directory data when the catalog is absent.
- `controlcenter_list_stacks`: read registered stacks from `stacks.catalog.json` and validate their `ellmos.stack.v2` manifests.
- `controlcenter_describe_stack`: describe the typed components, roles, policies, and warnings of one registered stack.
- `controlcenter_context_pack`: build a bounded, manifest-only context handoff for one registered stack at short, execution, or full detail; it never starts components or reads secrets or live state.
- `controlcenter_list_tools`: start local or profile-defined MCP servers and read their real `list_tools` output under bounded concurrency and response budgets; incomplete targets retain an unknown count.
- `controlcenter_find_capability`: rank stable, type-consistent native-binding claims from a hash-consistent System Explorer resolution; provenance and identity remain explicitly unverified, with no selection or execution authority.
- `controlcenter_tool_overview`: list resolution-bound claims while preserving separate declared, installed, configured, running, healthy, and observed axes.
- `controlcenter_assign_tool_bundles`: assign probed MCP tools to capability bundles.
- `controlcenter_list_bundles`: group local servers by capability bundle.
- `controlcenter_suggest_bundles`: recommend capability bundles for a task.
- `controlcenter_list_profiles`: list MCP profile files from the profile root (defaults to `~/.claude/profiles`, override with `ELLMOS_PROFILE_ROOT`).
- `controlcenter_suggest_profile`: recommend a profile for a task.
- `controlcenter_resolve_profile`: resolve profile inheritance, removals, and disabled servers.
- `controlcenter_switch_profile`: generate a resolved `--mcp-config` file and launch command.
- `controlcenter_audit_profile`: run initial profile policy checks.
- `controlcenter_build_catalog`: build a JSON catalog of local MCP servers, optionally including tool probes.
- `controlcenter_list_skills`: inventory deployed Claude Code skills and the source skills library.
- `controlcenter_find_skill`: match a task or intent against the scanned skill catalogue and return ranked candidates. Query with KEYWORDS/technical terms, not whole sentences — matching is purely lexical (no semantic search yet), so filler words in a natural-language sentence can outrank the correct hit. Scores are comparable only within one query.
- `controlcenter_resolve_semantic_route`: validate a caller-selected semantic role, expert, and persona against a provider-neutral map, verify endpoints against the live skill inventory, and preserve unresolved candidates as non-authoritative gaps.
- `controlcenter_list_plugins`: inventory installed Claude Code plugins and local ellmos modules.
- `controlcenter_list_locks`: list active `LOCK*.txt` project locks across the configured roots, under a wall-clock budget; an incomplete scan is reported as incomplete and names the roots it never reached. Read-only; requires `ELLMOS_LOCK_SCRIPTS`.
- `controlcenter_check_lock`: check whether one path may be modified, including locks inherited from parent directories, and report the effective lock with type, scope and expiry. Fails closed: unreadable path, missing configuration or an error yields `unknown`, never `clear`.
- `controlcenter_evaluate_permission`: report what the nearest `LOCK.permissions` register allows an agent to do at a path, precedence `deny > ask > allow > default`. A report, not enforcement; no register anywhere up the chain yields `unknown`, not `allow`.
- `controlcenter_list_decisions`: list pending user decisions by identifier, date, title, status and scope — deliberately not their question texts, options or recommendations. Reports when its index is older than its sources. Requires `ELLMOS_DECISIONS_ROOT`.
- `controlcenter_list_governance`: compose allowlisted decision, policy, strategic-plan and BYUM metadata from explicitly configured sources. The plan side reads the existing `ellmos.plans-register/1` index and omits paths, host variants and notes. Each source reports `available`, `unconfigured`, `unreadable`, or `invalid`; partial results stay partial, valid zero candidates stay zero, pointers are never dereferenced, and BYUM remains a pending advisory pointer without adoption or execution authority.
- `controlcenter_list_resources`: list rows from the host's resource inventory (systems and/or installed software), optionally filtered by host and/or type. Read-only mirror of `.SYNC/_inventory/inventory.db`; register authority sits with the ControlRoom programme.
- `controlcenter_describe_resource`: full row detail for one resource by its numeric inventory id, from the same read-only mirror.
- `controlcenter_list_available_tools`: list tools of backend MCP servers declared by the local root or a profile, without loading them permanently into the host.
- `controlcenter_invoke`: policy-gated execution of a single tool on an unloaded backend MCP server with automatic sanitization and audit logging.

## Install

```bash
npm install -g ellmos-controlcenter-mcp
ellmos-controlcenter
```

Dashboard:

```bash
ellmos-controlcenter-dashboard
```

Default dashboard URL: http://127.0.0.1:3737

## Audience

- Developers managing local MCP stacks who want visibility without manual JSON editing
- AI assistants (Claude, Codex, Gemini) that need to discover, catalog, or switch local MCP profiles programmatically
- Teams maintaining multiple MCP server setups and Claude profiles across projects
- Developers building on the ellmos-ai ecosystem or integrating FileCommander, CodeCommander, or n8n Manager
- Power users who want profile-aware policy audits and capability-bundle recommendations for their local AI tooling

- Good listing context: MCP control planes, local MCP server catalogs, profile management, policy audits, and MCP dashboard tooling.

## Target Personas & Comparative Advantage

- **Target Personas:** AI Infrastructure Engineers (fleet scaling, bundle management), Multi-Agent Runtime Developers (on-demand tool invocation via gateway without zombie processes), Enterprise SecOps (fail-closed policy loading, bounded result redaction, explicit HTTPS egress), and Local Homelab Automators (local dashboard, multi-agent lock awareness).
- **Comparative Advantages:** Dual control-plane + ephemeral connect-per-call gateway; dynamic on-demand tool calls (`controlcenter_invoke`) saving substantial context-window space versus static configurations; local-first administration without telemetry or background egress; explicit remote HTTPS boundaries; fail-closed policy file (`data/gateway-policy.json`); native multi-agent lock and permission-register introspection; permissively licensed direct dependencies.

## Important Files

- `README.md`: full English documentation with Target Personas and Comparative Matrix.
- `README_de.md`: German documentation with Zielgruppen and Vergleichsmatrix.
- `SECURITY.md`: bilingual security policy, no-telemetry/background-egress default, and explicit remote HTTPS gateway boundary.
- `THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md`: third-party open-source dependency licenses, audit summary, and notices.
- `MARKETING-LOG.txt`: local marketing, discoverability, search phrases, and governance log.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: version history and release logs.
- `server.json`: MCP registry metadata.
- `data/capability-bundles.json`: default capability bundle definitions.
- `data/policy-rules.json`: default profile audit policy rules.
- `src/index.ts`: MCP server entrypoint and tool definitions.
- `src/i18n/`: ControlCenter text sets and language switching.
- `src/toolCatalog.ts`: MCP client probes for real server tool lists, profile header forwarding, finite scan budgets, and cleanup.
- `src/mcpCatalog.ts`: reads `mcps.catalog.v1.json`, validates versioned capability tags, and joins it onto the directory scan; fail-soft on missing, unreadable, foreign-schema, or invalid catalogs.
- `src/bundles.ts`: capability bundle definitions, suggestions, and tool assignment helpers.
- `src/dashboard.ts`: local dashboard server.
- `test/controlroom.test.ts`, `test/catalog.test.ts`, `test/toolCatalog.test.ts`, `test/mcpCatalog.test.ts`, `test/semanticRouting.test.ts`, and `test/metadata.test.ts`: unit and integration coverage for the host-register bridge, canonical policy-registry validation, exact scalar governance allowlists, catalog, profiles, bundles, bounded tool scans, SSE header forwarding, versioned capability tags, strict map validation, deployed-only endpoint verification, deterministic collision handling, semantic-route validation, and metadata contract suites (257 tests passing in the full suite).
